headline: High risk of filesystem-based prompt injection and data leakage; shared write access also creates moderate conflict and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystem content, and Claude Code also uses MCP plus stdin/stdout, so attacker-controlled files or shared workspace artifacts can be treated as instructions. marketingskills explicitly builds on shared context, increasing the chance that Claude Code ingests B’s outputs. No direct shared channel is documented beyond files, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working directory or shared skill files, injected instructions can propagate from B to A.
IF Claude Code reads file contents as trusted task context, malicious content in shared files can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate working directories for A and B.
Mark shared files as data-only and strip instructions before handoff.
Disable or narrow MCP servers for the session.
Review any file-based prompts before either agent reads them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, while marketingskills reads and writes files in skill/context paths. Because both have filesystem access and A has broad network egress, sensitive repo or environment data can flow into B’s outputs or external calls in default workflows. The pairwise leakage path is documented by profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF A and B share a repo or workspace containing secrets or private source, B can read material A touched.
IF B’s outputs are copied back into A’s repo or prompts, sensitive context can be re-exposed externally through A’s network egress.
mitigations: Use separate repos or mount points.
Remove secrets from shared directories before running B.
Restrict A’s network egress during shared-workspace sessions.
Run B on sanitized copies of files only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and read the same cwd-style artifacts, so concurrent edits can overwrite each other. Claude Code also modifies git state and runs shell commands, while marketingskills writes skill/context files; that overlap creates default write contention even without explicit coordination. The blast radius is usually recoverable, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git branch or shared files, one agent can overwrite the other’s changes.
IF B writes skill files while A runs git operations, merge conflicts or stale reads can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate branches to each agent.
Serialize writes to shared files.
Use git locks or a single committer.
Keep B’s outputs in a staging directory.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed to build on shared context, so B may treat A’s generated content as authoritative. Claude Code can produce code, shell commands, and git changes that B may reuse without verification. This creates a plausible chain where A’s mistakes cascade into B’s downstream outputs, but no direct autonomous action like email sending is documented.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated files or prompts without validation, A’s errors can be amplified.
IF A writes incorrect code or commands into shared context, B may propagate them into marketing artifacts.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B ingests them.
Add a verification checklist for B’s inputs.
Keep generated artifacts separate from source prompts.
Limit B to summarizing, not executing, A outputs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code is documented as handling git credentials and source code, while marketingskills is a marketing-content agent with file-based context. The profiles do not show a clear residency or regulated-data mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is evident from the docs. The other agent is cited because the risk is about cross-agent handling of the same workspace data.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, retention and handling policies may diverge.
IF marketing content includes personal data copied from A’s repo, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Document retention rules for shared artifacts.
Redact personal data before handoff.
Use separate storage for credentials and marketing drafts.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies.
